adds.title: LGBTQ people in prison (Wikipedia; Mexico section)
adds.summary: Thin: Wikipedia's 'LGBTQ people in prison' article, Mexico section, records only one Mexico-specific policy: in July 2007, through the efforts of the National Human Rights Commission (CDHDF), the Mexico City prison system began allowing same-sex conjugal visits on the basis of a 2003 law banning discrimination based on sexual orientation, with visitors not required to be married to the inmate, applying to all Mexico City prisons. The article contains no data on trans-prisoner housing placement (birth-sex vs identity placement), special units, or solitary/segregation practice for Mexico.

records.note: No trans-specific prison-housing placement data found for Mexico within budget. Wikipedia full-text search surfaced no Mexico trans-prisoner article; the single relevant section ('LGBTQ people in prison', Mexico) documents the 2007 CDHDF-led same-sex conjugal-visit policy (sexual orientation, not trans placement). Prison Insider Mexico country profile (prison-insider.com/en/countryprofile/mexico) was fetched but returned a JavaScript shell with no readable prose on LGBTQI/trans prisoners, so no claims were taken from it. Adds: 1 verified (thin).
